highlights:
# An interesting observation: Nebius raised on-demand GPU rates on Oct 1. H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, B300 from $7.85 … | Chris Li · LinkedIn · 2026-10-13T00:00:00+00:00

...

An interesting observation: Nebius raised on-demand GPU rates on Oct 1. H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
Meanwhile, Anthropic launched Claude Haiku 5.5 on Oct 7 at $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens, for prompts up to 100K. Haiku 4.5 was $1 and $5. The arithmetic, counting output tokens only: $4.50 / $0.50 per million = 9M output tokens to pay for one H100-hour, or 2,500 tokens a second for the whole hour. At the old $3.85 rent and Haiku 4.5s $5 price: 770K tokens, about 214 a second.

Real serving is messier. Input tokens also earn, and a small model with good batching can clear 2,500 a second on one card. A model that needs the whole card for one replica has a harder time. Haiku is a closed model Anthropic serves itself, so nobody rents an H100 to run it. But this is the price open-model hosts get measured against now.

results.title: 【数据显微镜】再涨20％：GPU租金二度上调，算力缺口仍在拉大 - OFweek智能硬件网
highlights:
9月中旬，云计算服务提供商Nebius向客户发出调价通知，拟自10月1日起上调主要英伟达GPU的按需(on-demand)租金：H100由每小时3.85美元升至4.50美元，H200由4.50美元升至5.40美元，B200由7.15美元升至8.50美元，B300由7.85美元升至9.50美元，本轮涨幅约17%至21%。

这已是该公司年内第二次全面上调按需价格。若按两轮公开报价计算，以其首轮调价前的6.10美元为起点，B300每小时租金年内累计涨幅已达约56%。

价格连续上行的另一面，是算力供需缺口仍在拉大。中国信通院数据显示，2026年一季度，国内AI算力需求同比增长417%，同期有效供给增速仅为128%。从海外按需报价到国内合同金额，价格上行的链条正被逐段验证。

...

本轮调价并非孤立事件。今年5月宣布、6月1日生效的一轮提价中，Nebius已将H100由2.95美元/小时升至3.85美元，H200由3.50美元升至4.50美元，B200由5.50美元升至7.15美元，B300由6.10美元升至7.85美元，整体涨幅约29%。

两轮叠加，Nebius自身报价序列的绝对水平因此被逐轮抬升。按需价格值得单独拿出来看，在于它是新签合同与中小客户最直接的定价锚：按需价上移，意味着边际零售价格体系同步抬升。

浙商证券认为，这轮上调是“长约、短约、按需”价格全线上移的确认。更能说明紧张程度的是，涨价范围已溢出加速卡本身。同批调整中，纯CPU计算的AMD EPYC Genoa由0.012美元/vCPU小时上调25%至0.015美元，Genoa内存由0.0032美元/GiB小时上调约41%至0.0045美元，供给偏紧不只发生在GPU一隅，而是覆盖了算力基础设施的多个环节。

半导体行业的长期惯例是芯片出厂即开始贬值，如今这一规律在算力租赁环节出现了反转。英伟达官方口径印证了这一趋势：据英伟达首席财务官Colette Kress在2026财年第二季度财报电话会上的表述，Hopper系列GPU的租赁价格年内累计上涨20%，上一代的A100云价上涨近15%。

...

如果说海外按需报价反映的是零售端的即时供需，那么国内上市公司的合同金额，则是价格上行进入报表的证据。9月16日晚间，赛意信息发布公告称，公司与客户就高性能算力服务合同签订补充协议，将其中一份合同含税金额由36亿元调整为38.7亿元，两份合同合并含税总金额由64.5亿元调整为67.2亿元，增加2.7亿元。

...

公开信息显示，天阳科技于2026年6月与云粒智慧签署3.03亿元算力云服务协议，不足一个月后即签订补充协议，总金额上调至4.02亿元。2026年7月，行云科技全资子公司悦云树与客户就两份服务器租赁协议签署补充协议，合计上调租金28.79亿元，较原签约金额上调79%；同期，其另一全资子公司深圳行云与客户签署补充协议后，算力服务单元数由128个增至256个，合同总金额由10.14亿元提升至30.53亿元，其中已交付的8个单元每单元每月算力服务费较原合同增长21.21%，后续248个单元增长36.36%。金刚光伏则是解除原有约3.99亿元算力服务合同后，与新的交易对方签订约6.14亿元合同，两份合同服务期均为5年。

浙商证券将这一变化概括为定价逻辑的切换：2026年上半年，算力租赁板块的定价核心是供给端的拿卡能力，市场交易的是“谁能拿到GPU”；进入当前阶段，定价权正向需求端切换，市场开始验证“客户是否愿意为算力付更多钱”。国内算力租赁价格上调，已经进入公告验证阶段。云厂商的官方调价公告，为这条链条补上了中间一环。

3月18日，阿里云与百度智能云同日发布调价公告：阿里云对平头哥真武810E等算力卡产品上调5%至34%，文件存储产品CPFS(智算版)上调30%；百度智能云对AI算力相关产品服务上调约5%至30%，并行文件存储等上调约30%。

4月9日，腾讯云公告对AI算力、容器服务TKE-原生节点、弹性MapReduce三类产品价格统一上调5%。金山云则在7月对AI算力相关产品上调15%至50%。海外市场同步调整：亚马逊今年1月对用于大模型训练的EC2实例实施约15%的价格上调，谷歌云同月对数据传输、AI和计算基础设施等多项服务进行价格调整。

results.title: If you track GPU prices by checking vendor pages, last week would have looked like nothing happened. | Bobby Clay
highlights:
Across the nine providers we track, not one published on-demand price moved more than 1% between the October 4 and October 11 catalogs, and all four family floors held.

Every gap against the traded market moved anyway. On October 11 the lowest published H100 across those nine sat $1.25 above the Ornn Compute Price Index, a third-party index of traded prices rather than quoted or listed ones. On October 4 it sat $1.31 above. The published price never moved. The index did.

AWS also put B300 into its EU (London) catalog on October 11, from $27.19 to $27.67 per GPU-hour, as five listings for one machine. Same hardware, same region, same day. What differs is the operating system.
A flat week on the pricing pages was not a flat week.

Nine providers, every figure dated.

## 1. RunPod: Best Self-Serve GPU Cloud for Fast Pods and Serverless Inference

RunPod is one of the most practical answers for teams that want GPU access quickly without a long procurement cycle. Its pricing page lists per-second pricing for on-demand Pods, Serverless, Clusters, and Network Storage. It also separates Community Cloud and Secure Cloud, which is important: Community Cloud may be attractive for exploratory workloads, while Secure Cloud is the safer default for more controlled production work.

RunPod's public pricing page lists examples such as H100 PCIe from $1.99/hr on Community Cloud and $2.89/hr on Secure Cloud, H100 SXM from $2.69/hr and $3.49/hr, H200 from $3.59/hr and $4.59/hr, and B200 from $5.98/hr and $6.79/hr. Those rates make RunPod one of the easiest places to benchmark a new workload before negotiating a cluster.

## 2. Lambda Cloud: Best Simple Dedicated GPU Rental Experience

Lambda Cloud is a strong default for developers and AI teams that want dedicated GPU instances with clear instance shapes and a simple launch flow. Its current instance page says teams can rent NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, and A100 GPUs by the hour, launch in minutes, use UI/API/CLI workflows, and run multi-GPU instances.

Lambda's public table currently shows, for example, 8x NVIDIA B200 SXM6 at $6.69 per GPU-hour, 8x NVIDIA H100 SXM at $3.99 per GPU-hour, 8x A100 SXM at $2.79 per GPU-hour, and V100 at $0.79 per GPU-hour, with taxes excluded. It also positions the page around transparent pricing and no egress fees.

Choose Lambda when you need:

CoreWeave's pricing page exposes rows for NVIDIA GB200 NVL72, HGX B200, HGX H200, HGX H100, GH200, and supporting infrastructure. Its pricing structure is more detailed than a simple single-GPU marketplace, which reflects its cluster and platform orientation.

## 4. Crusoe Cloud: Best Cost-Focused AI Cloud to Put Beside CoreWeave and Lambda

Crusoe Cloud has become a serious option for teams evaluating AI-focused GPU clouds rather than general-purpose hyperscaler VMs. Its public pricing page includes H100, H200, B200, GB200-style references, storage, network, and support-related line items. Public page extraction on October 13, 2026 showed H100 around $3.90/hr and H200 around $4.29/hr in the visible pricing data, with additional storage and network rows that should be checked against the live quote.

...

The Azure Retail Prices API on October 13, 2026 showed Standard_ND96isr_H100_v5 examples at $98.32/hr in several US regions and Standard_ND96isr_H200_v5 examples around $110.24/hr in some regions. Those are VM-level prices, not a simple single-GPU marketplace rate, so buyers should divide by actual GPU count only when the full VM is fully utilized and then add storage, networking, support, and idle time.

...

## Price Comparison: Why the Cheapest GPU-Hour Can Lose

The easiest mistake in a best GPU cloud platforms 2026 comparison is to sort by hourly GPU price and stop. That misses the real bill.

Use this equation before choosing:

```
Accepted output cost =
  GPU runtime
+ idle time
+ queue delay
+ failed job retries
+ storage and snapshots
+ egress and data movement
+ orchestration and observability
+ support and engineering time
divided by accepted outputs

```

For training, accepted output may mean a successful checkpoint, benchmark score, or fine-tuned model. For inference, it may mean a completed request that meets latency and quality targets. For media generation, it may mean an accepted image or video, not just a completed render.

results.title: [SMM Analysis] Price Hikes Reach Desktop Devices; Computing Power Shortage Shows No Sign of Peaking - Shanghai Metals Market (SMM)
highlights:
This week, the computing power hardware market saw simultaneous shifts on both the supply and demand sides. On the demand side, the price-increase signal traveled down the transmission chain to the very end: monthly rental for 5090 eight-card servers in east China rose from 13,500 yuan/unit/month in early September to 16,000 yuan/unit/month, an increase of 18.5%. Rental prices and desktop AI device procurement prices moved up in tandem, cross-validating the growth and transmission of computing power demand. SMM believes this round of shortage has evolved from a one-way pattern of "demand transmitting down the chain" into a two-way squeeze of "demand pressing down while capacity pulls up.

...

In SMM's original analysis of computing power rental prices published in August (https://news.smm.cn/news/OUOCOCJSCPBTL4VHB4H5A33TSPBACMIPBRZWDVI), the transmission effect of computing power rental prices had already become evident. The rental price of 5090 eight-card servers, located at the very end of the computing power rental price transmission chain, is a key indicator reflecting shifts in the supply-demand relationship of the computing power rental supply chain. In the week following the end of China's 2026 National Day holiday, unusual movement occurred at the very end of the chain. SMM market tracking shows that on October 10, the rental price of 5090 servers in east China rose to 16,000 yuan/unit/month, up 18.5% from 13,500 yuan/unit/month in early September, reflecting the current undersupply in the 5090 rental market.

...

Since August, the SMM computing power rental price composite index (average price, yuan per card per hour) has shown a "three-stage" rise, with a total increase of about 26%.

The index pattern corroborates the spot signals from SMM market tracking: the stage high at the end of August corresponds to the first wave of high-end computing power price increases being transmitted to the mid-end, the September consolidation corresponds to the "buffer absorption" stage, and the jump after October is synchronized with first-line collection signals such as an 18.5% rise in monthly rent for east China 5090 eight-card servers, an 8%–9% rise in 5090 single-card prices over three weeks, and a 13% rise in DGX Spark channel prices over three weeks—after the buffer layer was breached, the shortage has become explicit at the index level.

The computing power demand for training and inference of the new generation of large models is first transmitted to the GB300 and B300 series; top-performance servers are expensive and supply is constrained, so demand spills over in turn to the H200, H100, and existing second-hand A100 series, then down to the Pro 6000 and 5090, and finally to the 4090. SMM's judgment in August was that "the mid-end computing power rental supply side has a buffer, and subsequent price transmission lacks momentum"; two months later, the buffer has been breached—the Pro 6000 server version single-card spot price in south China has risen from about 130,000 yuan in August (third-party market data) to 182,000 yuan in late September and early October (according to SMM), an increase of about 40%. The 5090 and Pro 6000, which took over the price increases from the upper tier, have themselves become scarce models: the computing power rental demand borne by these two devices, especially inference demand, continues to be transmitted downward after supply at that tier peaks.

highlights:

Rental pricing for an H100 rose from roughly $1.70 an hour last October to around $2.35 by March, according to Runpod's 2026 State of AI report.

That is close to a 40% increase in five months.

When a GPU hour costs more, an idle GPU hour costs more too.

Every straggler, stalled job or poorly utilised allocation now burns more money than it did before.

The waste has not changed.

The price attached to it has.

That changes the economics of infrastructure work.

An engineer who improves delivered throughput by 10% creates more value when every unit of wasted compute is more expensive.

...

If your existing estate is inefficient, the alternative may be renting additional capacity at the new market price.

results.title: Your 32GB Card, Gone: 41% Memory Hike | AIChieve
highlights:
Nvidia has reportedly stopped making the only consumer graphics card with 32 gigabytes (GB) of video memory [1]. That silicon is going to professional boards instead. Nine days earlier, on 1 October, the discount cloud firm Nebius raised its pay-as-you-go rental rates for the second time in three months. Its largest increase, 41%, landed on memory rather than on compute [3]. Neither move is about raw speed. In both, what is scarce and what sets the price is memory space.

...

The choice to build or rent has always rested on two numbers: the price of a card, and the price of an hour. In the past 30 days, one input moved both.

...

## By the numbers

- 84 GB vs 32 GB — Same core count: the professional card Nvidia listed in September carries about 2.6 times the video memory of the consumer card it shares a core count with. Nvidia has published no price for it [1][2].
- 41% — The memory line: Nebius lifted its rate on memory from 1 October, against 17% to 21% on graphics chips and 25% on some processor-only instances. Its 96 GB workstation tier did not move at all [3][4].
- $4,999 for 64 GB — The desk box inversion: Nvidia’s new half-size Spark machine ships on 23 October “starting at $4,999”. The 128 GB model that “launched at $3999 about a year ago” now lists at $6,950 [5].
- $3.47 — The H100 hour: that was the median on-demand rental across 41 providers in the week of 5 October, up 4.0% in four weeks and 16% in a year, even as the premium the big cloud firms charge narrowed to 75% [6].

...

One line in the rental data matters more to me than the price rises. The premium the big three clouds charge over the discount providers narrowed to 75% because the discount side moved up [6]. The floor rose. The ceiling did not.

...

My read is that this is a memory story wearing a compute story’s clothes. Three limits still apply.

First, the halt is a leak, not a statement. Nvidia has not confirmed it, has disputed it in private to at least one outlet, and cards already built can keep selling for a while [1]. The half I can stand behind is the pricing above it.

Second, renting has not closed. A one-year reservation still runs about 32% below on-demand, and a three-year about 49%. Spot capacity sits near 59% of the on-demand rate [6]. A team that will tie up capital, or put up with jobs dying mid-run, can still move its number down.

Third, the rises are not universal. Of 22 rental models tracked this year, 14 went up and 8 fell, and the 96 GB workstation tier did not move [4][6]. What repriced is memory-heavy gear, which is the same thing Nvidia is re-cutting its silicon to carry more of. TrendForce’s numbers from August, before this window, already had memory at 68% of major cloud providers’ capital spending for 2027, from 47% this year [8].

...

- The Big Shift: Nvidia reportedly stopped making its only 32 GB consumer card, to reserve that silicon for professional boards. It also listed an 84 GB professional card with the same core count and no price. In the same stretch, Nebius raised rental rates twice in three months, hardest on memory, at 41%.
- Why It Matters: Both halves of the artificial intelligence (AI) compute decision, buy or rent, now move with memory capacity rather than with compute. A 2027 plan built on price per unit of compute, or on today’s hourly rate, will come in low.
- What I’d Watch: three signals that will show whether memory has become this industry’s price index.
- The 84 GB card’s price: a price near the old consumer tag undercuts the line beneath it; professional money says the premium is deliberate.
- Whether the second rise holds: usage after two hikes in three months is the test of pricing power.
- The 32 GB resale market: a card that just stopped being restocked tells you what buyers think its replacement is worth.
- The Catch: the halt is an unconfirmed leak that Nvidia has disputed, and reservations and spot capacity still price below on-demand. The rent side has not closed. It has just stopped being the cheap answer by default.
